name: Software Requirements (SRS)
label: Software Requirements
description: Corpus-led Requirements Engineering model. Translates the Doc·Ray-grounded Zod SRS schema (plugins/software_requirements/schemas/software-requirements.ts) into an FDPM DomainProfile: a Software Requirements Specification decomposed into typed primitives (Specification, ScopeBoundary, Requirement, Stakeholder, Agreement, ChangeRequest, GlossaryEntry, Baseline) and relations (scope definition/exclusion, traceability, provenance, agreement, change control, baselining). v0.2 downgrades edge-existence rules from error to warning where nodes must be creatable before edges are wired. Grounding anchors preserved in descriptions as (SOURCE, sN): MRK=Managing Requirements Knowledge, OOSE=Object-Oriented Software Engineering, SE=Software Engineering.

categories.name: Specification
categories.label: Specification
categories.description: The SRS document, its shared vocabulary, and frozen baselines (OOSE s2068; MRK s23, s93).

categories.name: Scope Boundary
categories.label: Scope Boundary
categories.description: Positive scope, negative scope, exclusions, and non-goals that bound the SRS.

categories.name: Requirement
categories.label: Requirement
categories.description: Individual requirements — statements of what the system must do/be (MRK s93, s138).

categories.name: Stakeholder
categories.label: Stakeholder
categories.description: Parties holding requirements knowledge and the public agreement events between them (MRK s683, s3626).

categories.name: Change Control
categories.label: Change Control

primitive_types.name: Software Requirements Specification
primitive_types.description: Root document: '…constraints are stated in a document, called the software requirements specification (SRS)' (OOSE s2068). Section skeleton follows the template at OOSE s2519 (Introduction → Purpose → intended audience).

fields.name: project
fields.description: Project the SRS specifies.

fields.name: version
fields.description: SRS document version (semantic).

fields.name: date
fields.description: Document date (ISO-8601).

fields.name: authors
fields.description: Document authors.

validations.message: an SRS must name at least one author

fields.name: purpose
fields.description: '1.1 Purpose — Specify the purpose of the SRS and the intended audience' (OOSE s2519).

fields.name: intended_audience
fields.description: Intended audience of the SRS (OOSE s2519).

validations.message: declare at least one intended audience (OOSE s2519)

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Positive scope of the system under specification.

fields.name: out_of_scope
fields.description: Document-level negative scope statements: capabilities, behaviors, or concerns explicitly excluded from this SRS.

fields.name: non_goals
fields.description: Document-level non-goals that prevent readers from inferring unstated requirements.

fields.name: overview
fields.description: Optional document overview.

fields.name: references
fields.description: Referenced documents / standards.

fields.name: assumptions
fields.description: Assumed properties outside the system's control; RE covers desired properties AND constraints (MRK s94).

primitive_types.name: Scope Boundary
primitive_types.description: First-class scope boundary: positive scope, negative scope, exclusion, or non-goal. Keeps excluded capability separate from rejected or low-priority requirements.

fields.name: title
fields.description: Short scope-boundary title.

fields.name: polarity
fields.description: Whether this boundary includes capability in scope or excludes it from scope.

fields.name: statement
fields.description: Verifiable statement of the inclusion, exclusion, non-goal, or scope edge.

fields.name: rationale
fields.description: Why this boundary exists; prevents negative scope from being an unmanaged note.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: MoSCoW priority for respecting this boundary.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Lifecycle: proposed → analyzed → agreed → baselined → implemented → verified; or rejected.

fields.name: acceptance_criteria
fields.description: Evidence needed to confirm the boundary is respected.

validations.message: at least one acceptance criterion is required for a scope boundary

fields.name: verification
fields.description: V&V method for the boundary.

fields.name: source_reference
fields.description: Originating document, regulation, decision, or operator instruction.

fields.name: attributes
fields.description: Managed project-specific scope attributes — intentional extension point.

fields.name: open_issues
fields.description: Unresolved ambiguity about the scope boundary.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Informal annotations on the boundary.

fields.name: version
fields.description: Scope-boundary revision number.

primitive_types.name: Requirement
primitive_types.description: 'A statement of what the system must …' (IEEE glossary, quoted at MRK s93); prefer shall-form (MRK s140). Classified functional / non-functional / constraint (MRK s138, s94).

fields.name: title
fields.description: Short requirement title.

fields.name: statement
fields.description: A statement of what the system must do/be (MRK s93); prefer shall-form (MRK s140).

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Classification (MRK s138): functional / non-functional / constraint.

fields.name: nfr_category
fields.description: ISO/IEC 25010-style quality characteristic. Required when kind = non-functional [STD-1].

fields.name: rationale
fields.description: Why this requirement exists — externalized tacit knowledge (MRK s29). Unexplained requirements are unmanaged knowledge.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: MoSCoW priority; corpus fixes only that priorities are managed annotations (MRK s205) [STD-2].

fields.name: status
fields.description: Lifecycle: proposed → analyzed → agreed (public agreement, MRK s3626) → baselined (MRK s23) → implemented → verified; or rejected.

fields.name: origin_class
fields.description: First-class origin of the requirement. operator is primary evidence; ai_generated and derived are secondary provenance until promoted by the operator.

fields.name: provenance_rank
fields.description: Provenance weight assigned from origin_class: operator -> primary; ai_generated/derived -> secondary.

fields.name: origin_note
fields.description: Human-readable provenance note, including capture date, prompt/source, or derivation context.

fields.name: acceptance_criteria
fields.description: Concrete criteria enabling acceptance (OOSE s2079); at least one — an unverifiable requirement cannot reach 'verified'.

validations.message: at least one acceptance criterion is required (OOSE s2079)

fields.name: verification
fields.description: V&V method [STD-3].

fields.name: elicitation
fields.description: How the knowledge was surfaced; elicitation confronts unshared expertise (MRK s683).

fields.name: source_reference
fields.description: Originating document / regulation / ticket (provenance is requirements knowledge, MRK part I).

fields.name: attributes
fields.description: Managed requirement attributes — open extension point (MRK s5021).

fields.name: open_issues
fields.description: Acknowledged ambiguities / unresolved questions; ambiguity is managed, not denied (MRK s674).

fields.name: notes
fields.description: Informal annotations — first-class knowledge carriers (MRK s205).

fields.name: version
fields.description: Requirement revision number; incremented per accepted change (change control, MRK s5021/s117).

primitive_types.name: Stakeholder
primitive_types.description: A party holding requirements knowledge; elicitation must surface knowledge 'stakeholders immersed in their problem domain often fail' to share (MRK s683).

fields.name: name
fields.description: Stakeholder name.

fields.name: role
fields.description: e.g. customer, end user, developer, regulator.

fields.name: concerns
fields.description: What this stakeholder cares about (MRK s683).

fields.name: tacit_knowledge_notes
fields.description: Externalized tacit knowledge captured during elicitation (MRK s29, s683).

primitive_types.name: Agreement
primitive_types.description: 'The agreement to a requirement is public and made when programmers are looking into the eyes of the customer' (MRK s3626). Agreement is an EVENT with parties (→ srs:AgreedBy), not just a status value.

fields.name: date
fields.description: Date the public agreement was made (ISO-8601).

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional note on the agreement.

primitive_types.name: Change Request
primitive_types.description: 'Change requests are often used to refer to changes on requirements' (MRK s117). Controlled against requirement identity (MRK s5021).

fields.name: date
fields.description: Date the change was requested (ISO-8601).

fields.name: author
fields.description: Who requested the change.

fields.name: description
fields.description: What the change requests.

fields.name: impact
fields.description: Analyzed impact on related requirements (via trace links).

fields.name: resolution
fields.description: Change resolution.

primitive_types.name: Glossary Entry
primitive_types.description: Shared vocabulary; the corpus itself grounds 'requirement' in the IEEE standard glossary (MRK s93).

fields.name: term
fields.description: Defined term.

fields.name: definition
fields.description: Definition of the term.

primitive_types.name: Baseline
primitive_types.description: A frozen, agreed set of requirements (baseline as community anchor, MRK s23; agreement is public, MRK s3626).

fields.name: name
fields.description: Baseline name.

fields.name: date
fields.description: Date the baseline was frozen (ISO-8601).

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional note on the baseline.

relation_types.name: RelatedTo
relation_types.description: Verbatim corpus trace relation 'RelatedTo other requirements' (MRK s3133).

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional annotation on the trace link.

relation_types.name: DependsOn
relation_types.description: Requirement dependency; dependency types enable reasoning over relationships (MRK s357) [STD-4]. Must be acyclic.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional annotation on the trace link.

relation_types.name: DerivedFrom
relation_types.description: This requirement was derived from the target (MRK s357) [STD-4]. Must be acyclic.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional annotation on the trace link.

relation_types.name: Refines
relation_types.description: This requirement refines the target into greater detail (MRK s357) [STD-4]. Must be acyclic.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional annotation on the trace link.

relation_types.name: ConflictsWith
relation_types.description: Symmetric conflict between requirements; consistency must be resolved (SE s3207; MRK s357) [STD-4].

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional annotation on the trace link.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional annotation on the trace link.

relation_types.name: Satisfies
relation_types.description: This requirement satisfies the target (MRK s357) [STD-4].

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional annotation on the trace link.

relation_types.name: ElicitedFrom
relation_types.description: Provenance: the stakeholder from whom this requirement was elicited (MRK s683).

relation_types.name: ReusedFrom
relation_types.description: Provenance: the requirement this one was reused from; reused requirements carry their trace relations with them (MRK s3133).

relation_types.name: HasAgreement
relation_types.description: The public agreement event behind status 'agreed' (MRK s3626).

relation_types.name: AgreedBy
relation_types.description: Parties to a public agreement; requires at least the customer side and the builder side (MRK s3626).

relation_types.name: ChangesRequirement
relation_types.description: A change request targeting a requirement; accepted changes drive version increments (MRK s117, s5021).

relation_types.name: Baselines
relation_types.description: A baseline freezes a set of requirements (MRK s23).

relation_types.name: DefinesScopeBoundary
relation_types.description: The SRS defines a first-class scope boundary: positive scope, negative scope, exclusion, or non-goal.

relation_types.name: ConstrainsRequirement
relation_types.description: A scope boundary constrains how a requirement or candidate requirement is interpreted.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional annotation on the scope-to-requirement constraint.

relation_types.name: ExcludesRequirement
relation_types.description: An out-of-scope boundary excludes a requirement candidate or rejected/wont requirement from product scope.

fields.name: note
fields.description: Optional reason this requirement candidate is excluded.

relation_types.name: Includes
relation_types.description: Document spine: the SRS includes its scope boundaries, requirements, stakeholders, agreements, change requests, glossary entries, and baselines (OOSE s2068).

validation_rules.name: Non-functional requirement needs a category
validation_rules.description: Non-functional requirements need an nfr_category (MRK s138 classification + [STD-1]).

validation_rules.name: nfr_category only for non-functional
validation_rules.description: nfr_category is only meaningful for non-functional requirements.

validation_rules.name: Requirement must have a statement
validation_rules.description: Every requirement is a statement of what the system must do/be (MRK s93).

validation_rules.name: Requirement must have a rationale
validation_rules.description: Unexplained requirements are unmanaged knowledge — rationale externalizes tacit knowledge (MRK s29).

validation_rules.name: Requirement must have acceptance criteria
validation_rules.description: An unverifiable requirement cannot reach 'verified' (OOSE s2079).

validation_rules.name: Scope boundary must have a statement
validation_rules.description: A scope boundary must state the inclusion, exclusion, non-goal, or edge it establishes.

validation_rules.name: Scope boundary must have a rationale
validation_rules.description: Negative scope must be justified, not stored as an unmanaged note.

validation_rules.name: Scope boundary must have acceptance criteria
validation_rules.description: A boundary must be verifiable so scope enforcement can be inspected or tested.

validation_rules.name: Operator origin carries primary provenance
validation_rules.description: Operator-origin requirements are first-class primary evidence.

validation_rules.name: AI-generated and derived origins carry secondary provenance
validation_rules.predicate: field(origin_class) not in {ai_generated, derived} or field(provenance_rank) == 'secondary'
validation_rules.description: AI-generated and derived requirements are lower-provenance until operator-promoted.

validation_rules.name: Agreed-or-beyond status requires a public agreement
validation_rules.predicate: field(status) not in {agreed, baselined, implemented, verified} or has_outgoing(srs:HasAgreement)
validation_rules.description: Status 'agreed' or beyond requires a recorded public agreement (MRK s3626).

validation_rules.name: Baselined/verified requirement cannot carry open issues
validation_rules.predicate: field(status) not in {baselined, verified} or is_empty(open_issues)
validation_rules.description: Resolve or descope open issues before baselining/verifying (MRK s674 + s23).

validation_rules.name: Baselined/verified scope boundary cannot carry open issues
validation_rules.predicate: field(status) not in {baselined, verified} or is_empty(open_issues)
validation_rules.description: Resolve boundary ambiguity before treating the boundary as frozen or verified.

validation_rules.name: Out-of-scope boundary should link excluded requirements
validation_rules.description: An out-of-scope boundary should be linked to excluded requirement candidates. WARNING, not error: ExcludesRequirement edges are wired after the boundary node is created, so a hard error would make negative boundaries uncreatable.

validation_rules.name: Agreement requires at least two parties
validation_rules.description: A public agreement requires at least the customer side and the builder side (MRK s3626). WARNING, not error: AgreedBy edges are wired after the Agreement node is created, so this can only hold once parties are attached — a hard error would make Agreement uncreatable. Surfaced on the full-workbook validate pass.

validation_rules.name: DependsOn must be acyclic
validation_rules.description: Requirement dependency graph must be a DAG; a cycle (including a self-dependency) is a defect (SE s3207).

validation_rules.name: Refines must be acyclic
validation_rules.description: Refinement is hierarchical; the Refines graph must be a DAG (no self-refinement or cycles).

validation_rules.name: DerivedFrom must be acyclic
validation_rules.description: Derivation is directional; the DerivedFrom graph must be a DAG (no self-derivation or cycles).

validation_rules.name: Baseline must freeze at least one requirement
validation_rules.description: A baseline references at least one requirement (MRK s23). WARNING, not error: Baselines edges are wired after the Baseline node is created — a hard error would make Baseline uncreatable. Surfaced on the full-workbook validate pass.
